x: Herbert, Bill Lucas and Archie Bedford, they can feel well satisfied with their win, and this augurs well for our future prospects over the country and road.
We offer our hearty congratulations to Lew Bush and Archie Bedford on their recent marriages, and hope they will soon be back in training again once they can "escape" from their spouses.
Over our five miles course Field finished a good winner in 30 mins. 8 secs., and Archie Bedford ran well to finish a close second with Ches Walker also well up.
Archie Bedford, who won the London Transport 5 miles Cross Country Championship. Bob Readman, 1st in the M.P.A.A. 10 Miles Championship and 3rd in the National Police 10 Miles Championship.
Les Stokell ran his usual determined kind of race while Jack Brown seemed content to take matters easy in front of Archie Bedford, Steve Charlton and Jack Bragginton.

Archie Bedford now set about the field and running like one possessed, he caught the Blackheath runner and we were now 2nd to Thames Valley and Archie's time was a new record although slower than the 10.25 which Willie Nankeville did running for Walton A.C.

Lait, with Archie Bedford in third place, but the visitors had first two in the 440 with Jim Beaumont gaining a point for us. In the 1 mile, Derrick Burfitt and Jack Brown strode round in the lead and never looked like being troubled and they ran in together.

There was an entry of 13 teams and although we were without Len Herbert, Jack Brown and Bill Lucas, the latter being down with a touch of 'flu, we nevertheless managed to score a good win. Archie Bedford ran first for us and he set up a new course record with a time of 13 mins. 24 secs., beating the well-known P.

In the 880 yards both Alan Bishop and Archie Bedford failed to qualify for the final of this event The 220 yards saw Alan Sexton qualifying for the final, but he was obviously short of training and did not push it unduly when finishing in fifth place.

The 880 yards saw Archie Bedford and Jim Kennedy running for us but up against a strong Walton trio, which included Willie Nankeville, the A.A.A. mile champion, we had to be content with 4th place through Bedford, whereas Walton scored a “ maximum ” of 8 points for this race.

Odde was third in the 440 and Jack Brown won the 880 yards in 2 mins. 1.3 secs., with Archie Bedford in fourth place. Len Bishop was third in the 1 mile, but Charlie Smart surprised the locals by winning the 2-mile race, in which he beat Broughton, of Blackheath, in the fast time of 9 mins. 29.6 secs.
880 yards.—1, A.

Alan Bishop and Archie Bedford were first home in the 880 yards and Archie also ran a good race to win the 1 mile in 4.34. In the 2 miles our only two runners were Len Bishop and Ted Stimpson, whereas Dorking had J.

Thompson, the international runner, and " Mac " clocked 4 min. 33.8 secs., which is good going for a lad of his age. Ches Walker won the 440 yards, with Odde in second place, and Jack Brown won the 880, with Archie Bedford fourth.

Bartlett also ran in the sprint races, while Archie Bedford and Arthur Bruce turned out in the half-mile. Jack Brown and Bob Taylor ran for us in the 440, and Ray Tooby did the half for us in the medley relay.

Cope, was not competing, and Ches Walker won a good race from Archie Bedford, with Len Bishop running well for third place. Frank Kemp made a double of it by winning the 220 yards Junior race, beating Dave Marshall, who is the Surrey champion at this distance.

Archie Bedford was our next runner and he returned a time of 14.26 which beat the old record of 14.30 and then Bill Lucas took over for the final “ leg ” and he did 14.11 which was only beaten by Chataway of Walton, who put up a new record time of 14 mins. 2 secs. for this course of 2.94 miles.
Jack Brown, however, had other ideas and with a lap to go he went well ahead to win in 15 min. 19.2 secs., with Jack Bragginton just beating Archie Bedford for second place.
Archie Bedford ran well to give us the lead over the first “ leg ” but Len Adams had to relinquish this to the Reading runner although putting up third fastest time.
First man home was John Bromley, of the Police, and he was closely followed by Bill Lucas, with Steve Charlton and Archie Bedford also well up.

Archie Bedford ran well to hand over equal fourth on the first stage, especially as his opponents included E. Brown, the Mitcham lad, who won the recent South of Thames race, Bowen, of the local club, Nicholson, of Woodford Green, a most experienced runner, and Culver, of Essex Beagles, who last yea…

Although Jack Bragginton was our first man home in seventh position, Archie Bedford inspired the team by his forward running in the early stages, and the others were always striving to overtake him, which eventually Bragginton and Bob Taylor managed to do.

In both events Belgrave were well to the fore, as in the senior event Ted Stimpson, Bill Lucas, Archie Bedford, Vern Blowfield, Eric Herbert, Jack Bragginton and Steve Charlton were well up, and Ray Tooby and Bob Taylor were in the lead in the junior race.

Archie Bedford decided to have an outing in this race and, as expected, was an easy winner, with Reg Bolam second and Bob Taylor third, although the latter actually finished together with Ray Tooby and Doug Briggs.

Jack Bragginton just managed to beat Bill Lucas by the proverbial “hairbreadth” on the finishing line, and they were closely followed by Archie Bedford and Jimmy Wood, and the latter must think it strange to finish 15th and not score in the winning team.
The course was about 8 miles and the first man home was Archie Bedford, who beat a couple of Walton boys, with Len Adams and Denis Brickwood next home for us.
Among these were Vern Blowfield and Les Stokell, while Archie Bedford also stated his intention to do only one lap but then evidently changed his mind and ran well to finish in 4th position.
Our team all ran well with Archie Bedford surprising not a few by finishing in 4th place, while John Bromley proved his worth by being placed 8th out of a field of 226 starters.

Bill Lucas and Archie Bedford were the first two home and they were followed by two of our visitors. Vern Blowfield also took this opportunity to have a run out with the lads and we hope that next season we shall see him once again doing his “stuff” over the country.

Walker went off on the first leg and handed over in 2nd place one second behind young Pirie of S.L.H. and then Archie Bedford took us into the lead for Bill Lucas to consolidate our position so that Jack Brown had a comfortable run on the last leg to come home in 1st place, with T.V.H. second and Ay…

Len Herbert then exceeded our wildest hopes by not only catching his rival, but giving us a lead of 24 seconds, and Archie Bedford ran a gallant race to keep the lead, although Manley, of T.V.H., gained on him a little.
Thompson of Shaftesbury, a cross-country international, and Ray Tooby was close behind, with Archie Bedford in third place.
Archie Bedford ran a good race to beat Pudicombe of S.L.H. in the 2 miles, with Eric Herbert in third place, and the final points position was :—Belgrave H., 33; South London H., 16; Leicester, 5.

It was only through Bill " pepping " up the pace with a lap to go that the field broke up and this enabled Walker to use his stronger finishing powers to good advantage. In the 3 miles run we had Les Stokell and Archie Bedford, and they finished fourth and fifth, to score some useful points.
Gailly, running for Belgium and he is in the regular Army there. Archie Bedford won the London Transport 5 Miles C.C. Championship Race which was held at Wimbledon.
Alan Picton won the 600 yards with Maurice Jones second and Eddie Lacey third, while Arthur Bruce won the 3 miles run, with Archie Bedford second and Ken Stimpson third.
Walker allowed Green to hand over with him at the end of the third stage, but Archie Bedford, Eddie Short and Bill Lucas saw to it that we maintained our unbeaten record for this race.

A change of lead then took place when the Aylesford man went in front to be followed by Archie Bedford with Blackheath now in third place. Arthur Bruce was our next runner and he did well to beat the previous club record for this stage although Blackheath had now taken the lead again with Aylesford…

Archie Bedford, however, soon caught the leader and from then on we were always out in front. Len Adams kept up the good work and increased our lead and Bill Lucas took us further ahead to hand over to Mike Stearman 68 secs. to the good.
Charlie Walker won the individual race beating Alec Olney and Ted Manley with Bill Lucas in 4th place, Ray Tooby 7th and Archie Bedford 8th.

Our first man to finish was John Bromley 5th, then came Archie Bedford 9th, Len Adams 12th with Vern Blowfield 21st. The team race scoring four aside resulted thus—1, Aylesford Paper Mills S.C., 23; points; 2, Belgrave H., 47; 3, Cambridge H., 63; 4, City of Rochester A.C., 96; 5, Hythe A.C., 103; 6…

Archie Bedford finished third in the individual race with Vern Blowfield in fifth place, and then came Jimmy Wood 13th with Len Bishop 16th, and the latter just beat Tom Richards, the well known marathon runner.
With Braughton not eligible for a championship placing, owing to the fact that he is only 2nd claim to us, this meant that John Bromley took second place with Archie Bedford third.

Walker just beat Eddie Short for second place, and then came Jack Braughton 5th, Bill Lucas 7th, Archie Bedford 9th and Len Herbert 11th. All the first five were selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties race at York, and Jack Brown 7th in the Kent race and A.
Braughton 29th, Bill Lucas 44th, Eddie Short 53rd, Chas. Walker 55th and Archie Bedford 96th. Jack Brown 51st was running for Kent while a new member in A.
Alec Olney was first home followed by Charlie Walker, and then came Ray Tooby, Eddie Short and Archie Bedford who ran in together, just in front of A.
On the second lap we saw Charlie Walker, Eddie Short, Jack Brown and Archie Bedford running well together with Bill Lucas, our captain, acting as the whipper-in.
Hudson; 96, A.
We then ran "Ginger" Newell, who was a reserve that we had to bring in for Archie Bedford, who was injured, but what a "reserve" Ginger turned out to be!
John Bromley won the 2 miles run with Archie Bedford in 2nd place, and in the field events we had Luxon, Childs and Bill Sutton picking up a few points here and there.

Bill Lucas, Len Adams and Archie Bedford were other absentees, but quite a good field faced the starter. After Mike Stearman had shown the way over the first two laps, Jack Brown went in front and simply ran away from the rest of the field, and he lapped over half of them.
Our other members' times and placings were—11, A.

Notable absentees included previous winners in Vern Blowfield and Len Herbert, and we had Eric Herbert running in the Civil Service race on the same day. Len Adams, who has recently married, and Archie Bedford, also P.

We were not at full strength owing to the absence of Jack Braughton, Len Herbert, Archie Bedford and Len Adams, and did not expect to retain our team title, which we had held for the past two seasons.
Archie Bedford was first home in the British Workers' 5 miles c.c. championship, with Ron Mitchell in second place.
Jack Brown, John Bromley, Archie Bedford and Eddie Short were notable absentees, and the first three named were included in our Brighton team, with Eddie as 1st reserve.
Len Herbert was passed by Dunckley of the Poly. on the final leg, after we had been second to T.V.H. for the first three stages, and he was followed home by Archie Bedford, who had picked up a place.
We then had Archie Bedford on the 9th stage and he ran well to record the 2nd fastest time and almost caught the Poly. runner, who was now in 4th place.
Gordon was 3rd, with Ron Morrell 5th in the Senior 100 and John Burr and Archie Bedford were 3rd and 4th in the 1 mile, which was won in 4 mins. 25 secs. by Brian Hewson, of Mitcham.
The 1½ miles run saw "Lofty" Holden in the field as a "guest" runner, and he won in 6 mins. 54 secs. from Archie Bedford, with John Burr third.

Also at this meeting was the County Senior 6 miles track championship, which was won by Archie Bedford in 31 mins. 27.4 secs. In second place was our second-claim member, Bob Belmore, who did 31 mins. 33.4 secs.
Walker was first home in the 2 mile run in 9 mins. 42.6 secs., with Archie Bedford in second place, and T.
Kennedy was 3rd, with Archie Bedford 4th in the 1 mile, and B.

Charlie Smart who is now back in England for good - we hope - finished 2nd, with John Bromley 3rd. Then came A. Bedford,our junior D.Baulch,L.Herbert Bill Lucas, Dennis Brickwood, Len Bishop, Eddie Short, S.
The lead was held by Archie Bedford on the fourth stage to Merstham at which point we had 16 seconds over Essex Beagles and 28 over South London who had been slowly moving through the field.
The second venue was at Bognor again for a ten miles road race where we had A.

Archie Bedford on the 10th also did the fastest time of the day and brought us within striking distance of T.V.H. but Len Bishop on the last leg could make no impression on Eddie Ellis, T.V.H's International Steeplechaser, and the positions remained unchanged to the end.
Walker 10th, A.

The Cross Country Captain would like to see more of Len Herbert, Archie Bedford and Peter Hitchcock, to mention a few. Jack Goswell is waiting to see young Joe Scamell, Gordon Waddingham, Percy Wilson, and a contributor who calls himself "Spotter" adds his observations on what he "sees and hears" -
In the first few hundred yards it looked as if Archie Bedford was challenging the favourites for a place in the International team at San Sebastian.

Burr and A. Bedford had moved steadily through the field and were closely followed by Colin Collis who unfortunately was running for the "B" Team and our third man was slightly too far back to make up the points needed to win though he tried hard and only needed to have made one more place to do so.
Archie Bedford ran his usual "gutty" race and passed the Aylesford man putting Jack Brown off second 50 seconds behind Laurie Reed S.L.H. junior.
Archie Bedford ran well over the 4th stage but quite naturally was unable to cope with record runs by Norris and Sando and was relegated to 8th place.

Walker, Jack Brown and Archie Bedford who filled 4th, 7th and 9th positions respectively. Charlie Dabbs, still only a youth, took 10th place, a performance which should not pass unnoticed and it is hoped that his amazing improvement will continue over the next few years.

Walker, Jack Braughton, and Archie Bedford were among the non-starters and of those who were running only two were in full training. Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.

The position of the leaders was maintained down Copse Hill but it was noticeable that Archie Bedford, Charlie Smart and Denis Brickwood, who had all made a steady start, were making progress through the field.

Archie Bedford then took over but it was soon apparent that he was not fit enough to hold the opposition and slowly lost ground and places. At Mitcham we were back to 12th over a minute behind Tipton who had gone to the front.

In the senior event we were short of our best performers but it was good to see Archie Bedford once more in our midst and even more refreshing to see him running well enough to be our first man home in fourth place.

Archie Bedford returned for one of his rare visits and, by finishing fifth, proved he still has the capacity to gain a place in our first teams.

A spectacular return to form by Charlie Dabbs, a defiant battle against "father time" and injuries successfully overcome by Archie Bedford, and an extraordinary run by Clive Shippen were just a few of the highlights to emerge from this event, considered by some to be an unofficial "Brighton" trial.
He was relieved on the tricky Dale Hill stage by "veteran" Archie Bedford who put us well clear of the rest of the field. The last man, but by no means the least, was John Moore.

Shippen moved through well over the last mile and he was closely followed by Archie Bedford who had run steadily throughout. Bob Glover found out too late that one mustn't underestimate the finishing speed of those behind, especially when they include an accomplished half miler like Gerald Batty of Rochester!
Walker were well to the fore early on, and with Colin Collis, Archie Bedford, Len Bishop and Bob Plummer quite well placed, it seemed as if we might gain a team place in this well contested race.
Colin Collis, making a very successful comeback, was our first man home. He was closely followed by Eric Gebbett and Archie Bedford who both ran well in very difficult conditions.

Unfortunately, for a variety of reasons, Archie Bedford, John Davies, Colin Collis and Clive Shippen were unable to run, so with six to score and a "12 cup" in the offing we were able to start nine only.

Archie Bedford continued for the 'A' and did 24.30 to retain 10th position. Eddie Short, running for the 'C' remained in 13th place but Dennis Jones dropped the 'D' back to 14th.
Archie Bedford, although on the wrong side of forty, put up a plucky effort across Gatwick Aerodrome and, despite being forced to give way to Shaftesbury, can be said to have run true to form.

The Editors have been taken to task for withholding vital information re our increased membership. Both Archie Bedford and Eddie Short claim they were daddies before the issue of our last gazette.
